title: Food Access Research Atlas - SNAP-authorized Retailer Access Map Reference Guide

Updated: 7/27/2026

Contact: Alana Rhone

Definitions and Data Sources

This section provides definitions and data sources for the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP)-authorized Retailer Access Map’s (SRAM) census-tract level indicators as measured by Euclidean (straight line, “as the crow flies”) and network (vehicle travel along roads) distances.

General Tract Characteristics

General tract characteristics without access measurement

Population, tract total

Definition : Total number of individuals residing in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing.

Group quarters, tract with high percentage of population

Definition : A tract in which at least 67 percent of the population live in group quarters such as dormitories, military bases, assisted living or skilled nursing facilities, and other large institutions.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing.

Low-income tract

Definition : A tract with either a poverty rate of 20 percent or more, or a median family income less than or equal to 80 percent of the State-wide median family income; or a tract in a metropolitan area with a median family income less than or equal to 80 percent of the metropolitan area’s median family income.

Data sources : Census Bureau’s 2020–24 American Community Survey's census tract estimates.

Poverty rate

Definition : The share of the tract population living with income at or below the Federal poverty threshold by family size.

Data sources : 2020–24 American Community Survey's census tract estimates.

Median income

Definition : Median family income of a tract based on the distribution of family income, including families with no income.

Data sources : 2020–24 American Community Survey's census tract estimates.

Number of low-income people, tract total

Definition : Number of low-income individuals living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020–24 American Community Survey census tract estimates.

Urban/rural status

Definition : This variable indicates whether the population-weighted centroid of a census tract is in an urban or rural area. Urban and rural are defined in the Census Bureau urban area definitions, where rural areas are sparsely populated areas with fewer than 5,000 people or 2,000 housing units, and urban areas are areas with at least 5,000 people or 2,000 housing units. A census tract is urban if the geographic centroid of the tract is in an area with at least 5,000 people or 2,000 housing units; all other tracts are rural.

Data sources : In the Food Access Research Atlas (FARA), census tracts are classified as urban or rural based on the location of their population-weighted centroids relative to Census Bureau urban area boundaries, where centroids within an urban area boundary are urban tracts, and those outside the boundaries are considered rural. The Census Bureau's Centers of Population data provides pre-calculated population-weighted centroids using methodology documented by the Census Bureau. Their centroid calculations assume a spherical Earth model with latitude-based distance adjustments.

Housing units, tract total

Definition : Total number of housing units in the census tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing, reported at the census tract level.

Total child population

Definition : Number of individuals age 0–17 living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Total senior population

Definition : Number of individuals age 65 or older living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Total White population

Definition : Number of individuals who are White living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Total Black or African American population

Definition : Number of individuals who are Black or African American living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Total Asian population

Definition : Number of individuals who are Asian living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Total Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander population

Definition : Number of individuals who are Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Total American Indian or Alaska Native population

Definition : Number of individuals who are American Indian or Alaska Native living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Total Some Other Race/ Two or More Races population

Definition : Number of individuals who are not included in the White, Black or African American, American Indian or Alaska Native, Asian, and Native Hawaiian or Other Pacific Islander race categories or who identify as more than one race living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Total Hispanic or Latino population

Definition : Number of Hispanic or Latino individuals living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Total number of housing units without a vehicle

Definition : Number of housing units without access to a vehicle in a tract.

Data sources : 2020–24 American Community Survey census tract estimates.

Total SNAP housing units

Definition : Number of housing units receiving SNAP benefits in a tract.

Data sources : 2020–24 American Community Survey tract estimates.

Total veteran population

Definition : Number of individuals who are veterans of the U.S. Armed Forces living in a tract.

Data sources : 2020 Census of Population and Housing tract-level counts.

Tribal area, tract share

Definition : Percentage of Tribal area (Federally recognized American Indian reservations and off-reservation trust land areas, State-recognized American Indian reservations, and Hawaiian home lands) in a tract.

Data sources : The geographic Tribal area data are from Census Bureau geographic data on American Indian/Alaska Native/Native Hawaiian Areas (AIANNH), and include reservations, lands, statistical areas, and joint-use areas recognized as Federal, State, and Tribal entities. Tribal area in square meters is calculated at tract level and then divided by the total area in square meters of the tract.

Distance-Based Measures Summary Table

A summary table of distance‑based measures is provided below to offer a summary of thresholds, criteria, and distance types across measures. Readers can use this table to quickly identify the measures before reviewing the full definitions in subsequent sections.

STARS = Store Tracking and Redemption System, which has stores authorized to accept SNAP (Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program) benefits

Landscan = LandScan USA 2020 population density patterns

ACS = American Community Survey (ACS)

Census 2020 = 2020 Census of Population and Housing

Note: Asterisks (***) denote that the measure applies to all areas, regardless of whether a tract is urban or rural. In contrast, the 0.5-mile and 1‑mile thresholds in the other measures are used for urban areas, while the 10-mile and 20‑mile thresholds apply to rural areas.

Euclidean-based Distance Measures

Euclidean-based low-income and low-access distance measures

Euclidean: Low-income and low-access tract measured at 1 mile and 10 miles

Definition : A low-income tract with at least 500 people, or 33 percent of the population, living more than 1 mile (urban areas) or more than 10 miles (rural areas) from the nearest SNAP-authorized foodstore, calculated using Euclidean-based (straight-line) distance.

Data sources : The Food and Nutrition Administration (FNA; formerly Food and Nutrition Service) provided the complete list of food retailers authorized to accept SNAP benefits as of June 2025 from the Store Tracking and Redemption System (STARS) directory; LandScan USA 2020 population density patterns, which is produced by Oak Ridge National Laboratory; 2020–24 American Community Survey's tract estimates; Census Bureau 2025 urban area definition.

Euclidean: Low-income and low-access tract measured at one-half mile and 10 miles

Definition : A low-income tract with at least 500 people, or 33 percent of the population, living more than one-half mile (urban areas) or more than 10 miles (rural areas) from the nearest SNAP-authorized foodstore, calculated using Euclidean-based (straight-line) distance.

Data sources : STARS directory of stores authorized to accept SNAP benefits as of June 2025; LandScan USA 2020 population density patterns; 2020–24 American Community Survey’s tract estimates; Census Bureau 2025 urban area definition.

Euclidean: Low-income and low-access tract measured at 1 and 20 miles

Definition : A low-income tract with at least 500 people, or 33 percent of the population, living more than 1 mile (urban areas) or more than 20 miles (rural areas) from the nearest SNAP-authorized foodstore, calculated using Euclidean-based (straight-line) distance.

Data sources : STARS directory of stores authorized to accept SNAP benefits as of June 2025; LandScan USA 2020 population density patterns; 2020–24 American Community Survey’s tract estimates; Census Bureau 2025 urban area definition.

Euclidean: Low-income and low-access tract using vehicle access and at 20 miles

Definition : A low-income tract where at least one of the following is true: at least 100 households are located more than one-half mile from the nearest food store and have no vehicle access; or at least 500 people, or 33 percent of the population, live more than 20 miles from the nearest food store, regardless of vehicle availability. In the SRAM, the nearest foodstore is the nearest SNAP-authorized store, calculated using Euclidean-based (straight-line) distance.

Data sources : STARS directory of stores authorized to accept SNAP benefits as of June 2025; LandScan USA 2020 population density patterns; 2020–24 American Community Survey’s tract estimates; Census Bureau 2025 urban area definition.

Data sources : 2020–24 American Community Survey tract-level estimates.

Definition : An urban tract with at least 500 people, or 33 percent of the population, living more than one-half mile from the nearest SNAP-authorized store, calculated using Euclidean-based (straight-line) distance.

Data sources : STARS directory of stores authorized to accept SNAP benefits as of June 2025; 2020 Census of Population and Housing; Census Bureau 2025 urban area definition.

Definition : Number of individuals living more than one-half mile from the nearest SNAP-authorized store, calculated using Euclidean-based (straight-line) distance.

Data sources : STARS directory of stores authorized to accept SNAP benefits as of June 2025; 2020 Census of Population and Housing.

Once Euclidean (straight-line) distance to the nearest foodstore was calculated for each grid cell, the number of individuals living more than one-half mile from a foodstore was aggregated to the tract level.

Network-based low-income and low-access distance measures

Network: Low-income and low-access tract measured at 1 mile and 10 miles

Definition : A low-income tract with at least 500 people, or 33 percent of the population, living more than 1 mile (urban areas) or more than 10 miles (rural areas) from the nearest SNAP-authorized foodstore, calculated using network-based (road path) distance.

Data sources : STARS directory of stores authorized to accept SNAP benefits as of June 2025; LandScan USA 2020 population density patterns; 2020–24 American Community Survey's tract estimates; Census Bureau 2025 urban area definition.

Network: Low-income and low-access tract measured at one-half mile and 10 miles

Definition : A low-income tract with at least 500 people, or 33 percent of the population, living more than one-half mile (urban areas) or more than 10 miles (rural areas) from the nearest SNAP-authorized foodstore, calculated using network-based (road path) distance.

Data sources : STARS directory of stores authorized to accept SNAP benefits as of June 2025; 2020 Census of Population and Housing.

Once road network distance to the nearest foodstore was calculated for each grid cell, the number of individuals who are American Indian or Alaska Native living more than 20 miles from a foodstore was aggregated to the tract level and then divided by the total number of individuals in the tract to obtain the percentage of the total population who are American Indian and Alaska Native in the tract located more than 20 miles from a foodstore.
